newsitem.title: JAPAN: Three Japan financial firms to boost ties-paper.
newsitem.headline: Three Japan financial firms to boost ties-paper.

text.p: Fuji Bank Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd and Yasuda Mutual Life Insurance Co (Yasuda Life) plan to strengthen capital ties and business cooperation ahead of Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulation, a Japanese business daily said on Wednesday.

The scheme will include Fuji Bank's and Yasuda Life's planned purchase of two thirds of the subordinated bonds that Yasuda Trust is due to issue between July and September, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Yasuda Trust plans to issue 30 billion yen worth of subordinated bonds, the paper said, adding that Yasuda Trust would also ask trading company Marubeni Corp to buy 10 billion yen worth of the bonds.
The three financial institutions will assist each other by consigning each other certain areas of business to raise efficiency, Nihon Keizai said.
For example, Fuji Bank manages some of Yasuda Trust's foreign exchange operations as early as in the next business year starting April 1, 1998, the paper said.

The three companies plan to strengthen ties in order to survive increasing competition amidst Japan's deregulation in the financial sector that allows the establishment of a financial holding company, the paper said.
The three companies and Marubeni were not immediately available for comment on the report.
